vulnerability_analysis: The vulnerability is in the _reflectFee function where charity fee is subtracted from _rTotal but not from _tTotal (unlike burn fee). This creates an inconsistency between reflection supply and token supply. The rate calculation (_getRate = rSupply / tSupply) becomes skewed because rSupply decreases more than tSupply when charity fees are taken. This means each reflection unit represents slightly more tokens than it should, benefiting holders who aren't excluded from reflections.
attack_strategy: 1. Acquire some tokens to start with. 2. Perform transfers to trigger fee calculations with charity fees. 3. The charity portion reduces _rTotal but not _tTotal, causing the reflection-to-token rate to increase. 4. As the rate increases, our balance in token terms (calculated via tokenFromReflection) increases relative to others. 5. Repeat transfers to amplify the effect.
step_by_step_plan: 1. Get initial token balance from the owner or another holder. 2. Create multiple helper addresses to transfer between. 3. Perform a series of transfers between these addresses, each time triggering the fee mechanism. 4. Since charity fees reduce _rTotal but not _tTotal, the rate (rSupply/tSupply) increases with each transfer. 5. Our token balance calculated from reflections will increase as the rate goes up. 6. Verify the attacker's balance has increased after the series of transfers.
